background_notes.fact: If B⊆ℝ is nonempty and bounded, then a=inf B and b=sup B are finite, a≤x≤b for x∈B, and diam(B)=b−a. For η>0, B⊆(a−η/2,b+η/2), whose Lebesgue length is b−a+η.

background_notes.justification: Completeness gives finite extrema bounds. Every pairwise distance is ≤b−a; points of B arbitrarily near each extremal bound give the reverse supremum inequality (also when a=b). Positive η/2 makes both endpoint inequalities strict. Lebesgue length of the resulting finite open interval is its endpoint difference.
